text:
maria: seeing weird CA behaviour in eu-west: GPU nodepool scales up for pending jobs then immediately gets marked unneeded and killed within 90s. pods go back to pending -> repeat. anyone seen this?

sahil: yup — sounds like scale-down too aggressive + expander choice. which expander we running?

maria: default from the helm chart, didn't override. i think it's `least-waste`? not 100% sure.

devon: default in our chart was switched to `least-waste` last quarter for CPU-heavy workloads. for GPU burstiness that punishes long provisioning times.

maria: that makes sense. eu-west has longer node startup (~3-4m) because of image pull + GPU drivers. CA sees node idle for ~60-120s and nukes it.

anika: couple quick flags to try: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m`, `--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.3`, and `--max-empty-bulk-delete=1` so we don't nuke many at once. also `--scale-down-delay-after-add=15m` helps while nodes warm cache.

sahil: +1. also consider `--expander=priority` and set nodegroup labels like `autoscaler-priority: "10"` for cheaper-but-slower pools vs `autoscaler-priority: "20"` for fast-on-demand. that effectively biases selection without custom controller.

lee: from cost side, we can't keep long-lived warm nodes everywhere. maybe use a tiny warm pool in each region (1-2 nodes) and let autoscaler prefer them. we experimented with `min-nodes=1` for gpu pools in high-traffic regions.

devon: note: CA's `balance-similar-node-groups` can also cause churn if you have many heterogeneous ngs. we had a case where it moved pods to balance and then scale-down kicked in. if your pools differ in capacity/labels, try `--balance-similar-node-groups=false`.

maria: sharing current CA args from our kube-system deploy:
```
--cloud-provider=gke
--expander=least-waste
--scale-down-unneeded-time=1m
--scale-down-delay-after-add=1m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
```

anika: yep change those delays -> 10m+ and util threshold lower for GPUs. also `--nodes=0:10:gpu-pool-eu-west` is okay but maybe `0:6` until we validate.

sahil: another thing — watch for taints/tolerations and pod priority. low-prio batch jobs without priority class can be evicted quickly. set `priorityClassName` for important gpu tasks so CA treats them as non-evictable by default planning.

lee: we also added a small admission hook that annotates pods with `autoscaler-avoid` when they are startup-sensitive, to prevent them from moving during early boot. hacky but reduced churn.

devon: if you're seeing the "pod rescheduled immediately" loop, check CNI IP exhaustion/errors. sometimes kubelet can't attach ENIs quickly in constrained subnets, which prolongs Pending and CA scales up another node. logs: `Failed to allocate IP` in calico/cni.

maria: good point — we did hit subnet quota two weeks ago in same region. ok will: 1) bump scale-down times, 2) switch expander to priority + label priorities, 3) add tiny warm pool, 4) check CNI/subnet quotas. i'll run a small canary.

kube-deploy-bot: deploy noted: updated autoscaler args in staging (rollout started) :rocket:

anika: once staged, monitor `cloudprovider_node_provisioning_seconds` and CA metrics: `cluster_autoscaler_unneeded_nodes` and `cluster_autoscaler_scaledown_kills_total`. also add alert if scaledown_kills spikes > 5/min.

maria: thanks all. will report back with metrics and logs in this thread. :pray:
